acceptance_criteria.criterion: Status filter dropdown includes ACTIVE, ALL, READY, IN_PROGRESS, COMPLETE, BLOCKED, ARCHIVED
Default filter is ACTIVE (shows everything except ARCHIVED)
COMPLETE projects have an Archive button in the project list
ARCHIVED projects have Unarchive and Delete buttons
Clicking Archive transitions project to ARCHIVED with confirmation dialog
Clicking Unarchive transitions project back to COMPLETE
Archived project rows have muted/dimmed visual styling with grey ARCHIVED badge
Config view includes Auto-archive after N days numeric input
Project detail view shows archive banner with unarchive button for archived projects
All archived project data remains fully viewable in detail view
Project list shows 'Archived' badge for ARCHIVED projects
ACTIVE filter (default) hides ARCHIVED projects; ALL filter shows them
Archive button appears on COMPLETE projects; unarchive button appears on ARCHIVED projects
Project detail page shows archive banner for ARCHIVED projects with unarchive action
Config page exposes auto_archive_days field (numeric, 0 = disabled)

app.js: archiveProject/unarchiveProject API helpers, default filter ACTIVE, applyFilter ACTIVE/ALL logic, archive/unarchive row buttons, filter dropdown update, archive/unarchive event handlers, auto_archive_days config field with validation, project detail archive banner with inline unarchive action.

comments.note: app.js is a large single-file vanilla JS application (~1460 lines). As new features accumulate the file will become increasingly difficult to navigate. A module split would significantly aid maintainability (out of scope for this WP).
renderConfig() mixes HTML string concatenation with post-render DOM wiring — consistent with the rest of app.js, no action needed.

summary: All 15 ACs verified in source code. Updated 10 initially-unmet ACs to met: true after code inspection.
Filter dropdown: 7 options (ACTIVE, ALL, READY, IN_PROGRESS, COMPLETE, BLOCKED, ARCHIVED). Default filterValue='ACTIVE'. ACTIVE logic: hide rows where status==='ARCHIVED'.
Archive button: rendered for p.status === 'COMPLETE' with confirm() confirmation dialog. Unarchive button: rendered for p.status === 'ARCHIVED'. Delete button: rendered for COMPLETE or ARCHIVED.
styles.css: .badge-archived (grey badge), tr[data-status="ARCHIVED"] opacity rule (muted rows), .info-banner with light/dark variants.
Project detail view: archive banner conditionally rendered when meta.status === 'ARCHIVED', with inline Unarchive button wired to API.unarchiveProject().
Config view: auto_archive_days numeric input rendered, value saved via API.updateConfig(). Default display value is 6 when config value is null.

KNOWN REGRESSION (by WP-007, to be fixed by WP-008): app.js render() expects a plain array from GET /api/projects but the endpoint now returns a paginated envelope. Project list page is broken until WP-008 is delivered.

comments.note: REGRESSION (by design, pending WP-008): GET /api/projects now returns a paginated envelope { projects, total, page, limit, total_pages, status_counts } after the WP-007 implementation. app.js load() still does API.getProjects().then(fn(projects) => render(projects)) and render() calls buildTable(projects) which invokes projects.length and sortProjects().slice(). This will throw at runtime because the envelope is not an array. The project list page is currently broken. This is the expected pre-condition for WP-008 and does not constitute a WP-005 defect, but it must be fixed before the feature can be validated end-to-end.

All 15 acceptance criteria are met. The 10 criteria initially left as met: false by the developer scaffold were all verified as implemented: filter dropdown has all 7 required options, default filterValue='ACTIVE', archiveBtn/unarchiveBtn/deleteBtn wiring is correct, confirm() dialog on archive, .badge-archived and tr[data-status=ARCHIVED] opacity rules in styles.css, .info-banner archive banner in detail view, auto_archive_days numeric input in config view.

summary: Code review PASS for gui/public/app.js and gui/public/styles.css (Frontend Archive UX).

Filter dropdown correctly exposes all 7 required options (ACTIVE, ALL, READY, IN_PROGRESS, COMPLETE, BLOCKED, ARCHIVED). filterValue initialized to 'ACTIVE' before first render — ARCHIVED projects hidden by default without any race condition.
applyFilter() logic is correct: ACTIVE mode excludes only ARCHIVED rows, ALL shows everything, specific-status mode does exact match. Client-side filtering is consistent with existing pattern.

Archive button conditional (p.status === 'COMPLETE' only), unarchive button (p.status === 'ARCHIVED' only), delete button (COMPLETE or ARCHIVED). All three are correctly mutually exclusive with respect to their primary action.

Archive action uses confirm() dialog with descriptive message before calling API.archiveProject(). On success/failure, reloads list or alerts. Unarchive skips confirmation (reversible action — appropriate UX decision).
Detail view archive banner rendered conditionally on meta.status === 'ARCHIVED'. Inline Unarchive button wired to API.unarchiveProject(slug) with re-render on success.

Config form: auto_archive_days input has min=0, step=1, parseInt validation plus isNaN/negative guards. Default display value 6 is consistent with server default. Saves via API.updateConfig together with other config fields.

styles.css: .badge-archived is grey (light + dark variants). tr[data-status='ARCHIVED'] opacity rule visually dims rows. .info-banner with light/dark theme variants. statusBadge() auto-generates 'badge badge-archived' from the ARCHIVED status string — no hardcoding needed.
All user-facing strings are passed through escapeHtml() before insertion into innerHTML. Slug values in href/data attributes are URL-encoded or HTML-escaped as appropriate. No XSS risk observed.
All 15 ACs are met.
Known regression (WP-007 produces paginated envelope, WP-005 load() still passes raw response to render(projects)): tracked, expected pre-condition for WP-008. Not a WP-005 defect.

comments.note: statusBadge() generates class names dynamically via status.toLowerCase().replace(/_/g, '-'), producing 'badge badge-archived' for ARCHIVED. This correctly matches the .badge-archived CSS rule — no hardcoding needed and future statuses auto-pick up badge styling if a matching CSS class exists.

load() in renderProjectList passes the API response directly to render(projects). After WP-007 the response shape changed to a paginated envelope { projects, total, ... }, so render() will throw at runtime (projects.length on an object). This is a known, tracked pre-condition for WP-008 — not a WP-005 defect — but end-to-end functionality is blocked until WP-008 lands.

Config form validates auto_archive_days with parseInt(value, 10) + isNaN/negative guards before saving. The fallback default of 6 when config.auto_archive_days is null matches the server-side default. Input has min=0 and step=1 attrs for HTML5 constraint validation as a secondary guard.
